title: Sitka: an open-source exoskeleton that works with your body
description:
Sitka is an open-source exoskeleton that works with your body instead of fighting it. Your bones carry the weight; springs, clutches and cable tendons do what your muscles do, and one small motor helps only where you need it.

The numbers (counted part by part in the parts list, not guessed):
- Seat + back starter kit: 6.31 kg (about 14 lb). About $1,925 a set in a batch of 10 (estimate), $2,671 for the first one-off build.
- Full body (hips, ankles, shoulders, one motor): 10.25 kg, $5,049 for the first build.
- About 175 printer hours for the whole body on a Bambu X1C / P1S class printer.
These are design targets, not yet measured on a prototype.

Everything is open: the CAD, the math, every part with its price.
Code, CAD and docs: https://github.com/nicedreamzapp/sitka
Parts list and cost: https://github.com/nicedreamzapp/sitka/blob/main/PARTS_LIST.md

Footage is rendered from the real CAD in Blender. The wearer is a digital human (MakeHuman / MPFB 2, CC0) driven by real motion capture.

Credits
Motion capture: CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database, http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/ (walk 35_01, run 35_17, sit and stand 86_09, stoop lift 115_01, stairs 13_35). The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The database was created with funding from NSF EIA-0196217.
Running shoes by punkduck (MakeHuman community), CC-BY 4.0.
HDRIs and textures: Poly Haven (CC0).
Music: Star Jumps Coach (instrumental), made with Song Forge, from Body Movin'.

Come build one with us.
